title: Safe handling of abstract type object types.
summary: Mypy always allows instantiating (calling) type objects typed as type[t], even if it is not known that t is non-abstract, since it is a common pattern to create functions that act as object factories (custom constructors). Therefore, to prevent issues described in the above section, when an abstract type object is passed where type[t] is expected, mypy will give an error. mypy enables this error code by default.

title: Check that type arguments exist.
summary: If you use --disallow-any-generics, mypy requires that each generic type has values for each type argument. For example, the types list or dict would be rejected. mypy does not enable this error code by default. Use --enable-error-code type-arg to enable it.

title: Check type variable values.
summary: Mypy checks that value of a type variable is compatible with a value restriction or the upper bound type. mypy enables this error code by default.

title: Check TypedDict items.
summary: When constructing a TypedDict object, mypy checks that each key and value is compatible with the TypedDict type that is inferred from the surrounding context. mypy enables this error code by default.

title: ReadOnly key of a TypedDict is mutated.
summary: mypy enables this error code by default.

title: Check TypedDict Keys.
summary: When constructing a TypedDict object, mypy checks whether the definition contains unknown keys, to catch invalid keys and misspellings. On the other hand, mypy will not generate an error when a previously constructed TypedDict value with extra keys is passed to a function as an argument, since TypedDict values support structural subtyping ("static duck typing") and the keys are assumed to have been validated at the point of construction. mypy enables this error code by default.
